extracted.intended_audience: public relations / corporate communications professionals managing crisis communications and press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and actionable standards for preparing and issuing press releases (and related communications) during a crisis, including pre-crisis preparedness, timeliness, content, stakeholder engagement, and post-crisis follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: All known facts disclosed; no selective omission; acknowledge what's not yet known; update when new facts emerge; correct misstatements promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full and truthful disclosure is required. Do not omit selected facts to shape perception; explicitly say what remains unknown and commit to updates as facts develop; promptly correct errors or misstatements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove it with action
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific corrective steps with a timeline for each action, named accountability owners, independent verification, and public reporting of progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications must pair words with concrete, verifiable actions: spell out what will be done, when it will be done, who is accountable, how results will be independently verified, and how progress will be reported publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple feedback channels; reflect stakeholder concerns in the response; make adjustments based on input; enable two-way communication; plan for long-term engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design communications to solicit and incorporate stakeholder feedback (not one-way broadcasts). Use several channels, show evidence that concerns influenced decisions, and maintain ongoing engagement rather than a single statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage for tomorrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on long-term reputation; don't sacrifice future for today's optics; build durable trust; acknowledge systemic issues if present; commit to policy/practice changes that prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions and messaging should prioritize sustainable trust and future consequences over short-term image management. When problems are systemic, acknowledge them and commit to structural fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct PR as if the entire company depends on it
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat crisis communications with the utmost seriousness and resources, as though the company's survival hinges on the quality of PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate senior attention, cross-functional coordination, and necessary resources to communications work; avoid treating PR as an afterthought during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company character is expressed by people
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the company's true character is shown through the words and actions of its people and representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select spokespeople and craft messages that reflect authentic values and behavior; ensure staff conduct and statements embody the organization's commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: remain calm, patient, and good-humored
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a calm, patient, and good-humored tone where appropriate during crisis communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone matters — avoid panic, defensiveness, or excessive flippancy. A measured tone can help maintain credibility and stakeholder trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-crisis preparedness: crisis playbook updated annually
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and update a crisis playbook on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep documented plans current so teams can follow tested processes during an actual crisis; annual updates ensure relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-crisis preparedness: spokesperson trained
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure designated spokespeople are trained prior to crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular media and crisis training prepares spokespeople to communicate clearly, honestly, and consistently under pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-crisis preparedness: stakeholder maps current
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain current stakeholder maps to understand who must be informed and engaged during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate stakeholder mapping enables targeted communications and prioritization of outreach during an incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-crisis preparedness: dark site ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a 'dark site' (pre-built crisis web page) prepared and ready to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preconfigured site allows rapid publication of official information and minimizes confusion from unofficial sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-crisis preparedness: relationships with media established
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain established relationships with media prior to a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivated media relationships facilitate quicker, clearer distribution of accurate information and can improve coverage quality during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness/responsiveness standards during crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge within 2 hours; issue an initial release within 24 hours; provide a substantive update within 72 hours; report resolution in weeks; honor long-term commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and meet explicit timing expectations for communications: immediate acknowledgment to signal attention, a fuller initial release within a day, substantive updates within a few days, and ongoing reporting through resolution and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: During-crisis: name accountability and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify accountability owners and provide timelines for corrective steps as part of crisis communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming responsible parties and specific timelines increases credibility and allows stakeholders to track progress and hold the organization to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: During-crisis: independent verification and public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use independent verification mechanisms and publicly report progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party verification and transparent public updates reduce skepticism and substantiate claims of corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis: audit lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an audit to capture lessons learned after the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically review response performance to identify strengths and gaps for future improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis: update playbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate lessons learned into the crisis playbook and update it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the playbook evolves based on actual experience so future responses are improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis: restore stakeholder trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in actions and communications aimed at restoring stakeholder trust after resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust restoration is an explicit post-crisis objective, requiring sustained outreach, transparency, and fulfillment of commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis: track sentiment over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor stakeholder sentiment over time as part of post-crisis recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentiment tracking to measure effectiveness of recovery efforts and to guide further engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis: make systemic changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement systemic policy or practice changes that prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond surface fixes, commit to structural reforms where issues are root-cause systemic to rebuild credibility and reduce future risk.
